newsitem.title: UK: Euromarkets hold gains, US data as expected.
newsitem.headline: Euromarkets hold gains, US data as expected.

text.p: European share markets were generally steady, holding their morning gains as U.S. second quarter real GDP figures came in on expectations.
Wall Street opened mixed on the data, failing to match the 13/32 gain in long U.S. government bonds -- taking yields down to 6.85 percent -- and failing to provide direction for Europe.
By midafternoon London's blue chip FTSE 100 index was up around 18 points, a few points off the day's highs, before slipping to about 11 ahead.
The market had been supported by a strong performance in gilts and a rally in British drug stocks sparked by U.S. buying overnight.
In Paris, French shares stayed firm in early afternoon trading, sustained by continued firmness in bond markets, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up around two points. Volume was around two billion francs.

Italian stocks and bonds soared on a wave of euphoria that tougher than expected 1997 budget-cutting measures will thrust the nation into the front line for membership of the single European currency.
Analysts said bonds, the lira and shares responded positively to the centre-left government's determination to adhere to strict financial discipline.

In early trading, Italian domestic bonds surged to touch historic highs, the lira continued firm after touching its highest level against the German mark since early August 1994 in late Thursday trading.
Shares on the Milan bourse were driven higher with the all-share Mibtel index up 2.34 percent at 10,080 and the Mib30 index of Italy's 30 biggest companies up 2.65 percent.

In Frankfurt, German shares closed bourse floor trade slightly lower on a mild bout of profit-taking following recent moves up towards record-highs, but the underlying tone was helped by continued dollar strength.
DAX futures eased, but were off their lows. The 30-share DAX blue chip index closed 7.51 points lower at 2,659.04 on modest volumes, while the electronically traded IBIS DAX was down 6.8.
In currencies, the dollar was held off its highs by selling at top levels around 1.52 marks, after the U.S. real GDP figures failed to surprise.

Analysts said the market would now be looking at the minutes of the August 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, due tonight, to see whether the U.S. Federal Reserve was biased towards tightening or easing U.S. monetary conditions.
And players were already gearing up for the most important indicator, U.S. non-farm payrolls, due to appear next Friday. This will dominate the markets next week, traders and analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5221 marks and 110.73 yen by 1430 GMT, up slightly from late Thursday's European level of 1.5209 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 11.9 points at 3,945.1
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 0.78 points at 2,104.92.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 7.51 points at 2.659.04. PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed 40 cents firmer from the morning at $380.70. Silver was three cents firmer at $4.92, following gold. Platinum was down five cents at $385.45, off the day's lows. Palladium was firmer at $118.50, up 75 cents.
